findings.summary: After the narrowing, no scan covers the reading's title, summary and criterion text on their way into commit messages and the pull request title. The plan defers this, which is reasonable, but the user must see it.
findings.evidence: reading.rs:2709-2738 shows `reading_text_fields` is today the only place title, summary and criterion texts are scanned. The plan's own survey shows that text reaches landing commit messages and the pull request title (run/close.rs `landing_body`, `closing_subject`; run/mod.rs to gh/early.rs). The host squash-merges, so that text can become the commit on main. Fix: Keep the deferral, which is in line with the request's premise and the 'small' default. Make sure the open question reaches the user as a proposed follow-up job, not only as a line in the D153 Tradeoff. If the user would rather close the gap in this job, sanitizing at the sinks with `plain_boundary_text` is the right fix. Re-scanning prose in the reading is not.

findings.summary: Two test-only files outside the deliverables are justified departures.
findings.evidence: run_pin_tests.rs:1730-1739 sets only `summary` and asserts the error contains 'summary', so it fails once the narrowing lands. The corpus has no boundary-word form (INPUT_FORMS at refusal_corpus.rs:70-87 holds 16 tags, none for boundary words). Fix: No change to the plan is needed. In the producer's output, name both files as departures with these reasons.

findings.summary: The plan does not say whether the new Create deliverable replaces the base deliverable or is added beside it.
findings.evidence: `base_reading` (refusal_corpus.rs:139) already has the deliverable `docs/guide.md` modify. The plan says 'Create docs/<word>.md' without saying which. Fix: Say that the case adds the Create deliverable and keeps docs/guide.md, so the only problem is the word. Assert that the refusing check is `check_boundary_and_repo_files`.

summary: I read the code in the snapshot to check the plan's claims, and they hold. `reading_text_fields` (reading.rs:2709) is called only by `check_boundary_and_repo_files` (reading.rs:2771). That check scans every prose field, every criterion and every deliverable path, so the change belongs in that helper, where the fault starts. The test fixtures named in the plan exist: `governed_reading`, `banned_word`, `banned_fragment`, `files_at_head` and `reading_with_deliverable`. So do the end-to-end test at run_pin_tests.rs:1718 (it asserts a refusal over the summary and would break), the content-kind criterion 0 in that file's reader fixture, the corpus `INPUT_FORMS` of 16, the `case`/`base_reading` builders, and D152 as the latest decision. Each demonstration calls `check_reading_acceptance`, `Athena::ask` or the corpus harness, all of which exist, and each would fail under the old scan or if the narrowing went too far. Keying the scan on criterion kind is the only signal the `Criterion` struct carries. The plan names both edge cases of that choice and does not overstate the backstops. The commit-text gap is real. The plan names it honestly and defers it as an open question, which fits the request's stated premise and the 'small' default. No athena.toml field is added, the work fits one producer run, and no external service is called. I found no blocker or major issue, so the verdict is accept.
